source_snapshot.items: BMC Stress - Masses of BMC Load
source_snapshot.procedure: Continuously send IPMI OOB and IB commands such as `mc info`, `sel elist` and `sdr elist` while repeatedly displaying dmesg for 12 hours; generic log clearing is stated.
source_snapshot.criteria: BMC remains functional and no stress-caused BMC SEL or OS event errors occur.
source_snapshot.script: No Script; 30 attended and 720 machine minutes.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; proposes an unspecified-count OOB-only `mc info` loop with hardcoded cipher and command-line password, suppresses stdout, and leaves the 12-hour in-band path, rate and health/event acceptance unimplemented.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION at HIGH risk; isolated management path, OOB/in-band allowlist, bounded load, per-command latency/results, session/health monitoring and independent recovery are required.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Recognizes BMC traffic stress and management-network risk, but its loop tests only one OOB request type and cannot establish dual-path command coverage, SEL/SDR behavior or 12-hour functional stability.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly constrains the workload to approved read-only commands with rate/session controls, continuous BMC/OS monitoring and fail-closed recovery.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code/source search found no earlier V3.1 record for this identity.
historical_reviews.v3_1: OOB and IB are treated as distinct BMC access paths in this row: each request must be labeled by path and command class so a healthy OOB channel cannot hide in-band failure. Read-heavy SEL/SDR requests can consume BMC sessions and service CPU; response latency distribution and completion codes are primary evidence, not just loop duration.

original_test_intent: Validate 12-hour BMC stability under sustained approved OOB and in-band IPMI read load while BMC functionality, SEL/SDR access and OS event health remain intact.
original_method: On an isolated dedicated SUT/BMC, confirm OOB and in-band interfaces, calibrate owner-approved read-only `mc info`, `sel elist` and `sdr elist` rates/concurrency, run bounded 12-hour generators with per-request path/timestamp/latency/completion capture, continuously preserve incremental dmesg/SEL plus BMC reachability/session health, and stop both paths on degradation without tight reconnect loops.
manual_activity: The BMC/network owner defines OOB and in-band endpoints, command mix, rate/concurrency/session limits, 12-hour window, latency/error thresholds and recovery, supervises management health and decides the verdict.
required_inputs: Approved read-only command allowlist and mix
Request rate, concurrency, burst and session limits
Dedicated management network and route isolation
safety_requirements: Do not run unbounded or zero-delay generators
Do not use write, reset, power, credential or firmware commands
Do not flood a shared production management network
Do not hardcode an unapproved cipher or put passwords on command lines
Preserve rather than clear SEL and OS logs
Calibrate rate before the long soak
Reserve sessions/capacity for monitoring and recovery
Stop on latency/error/session threshold, path loss, event error or BMC instability
Do not tight-loop reconnect or auto-retry after degradation
agent_execution_scope: Verify BMC identity, both paths, isolation and command safety
Capture SEL/SDR/FRU, network/session, reachability and OS baseline
Calibrate approved request mix and rate
Run bounded path-labeled generators for 12 hours
Collect every latency/completion plus periodic health/events
Enforce cross-path stop conditions and preserve failure chronology
Verify normal BMC latency/function and sessions after stop
engineer_actions: Approve path semantics, command mix and load envelope
Approve secure authentication/cipher and management isolation
Approve thresholds, maintenance and independent recovery
Monitor BMC capacity and authorize abort/recovery
Resolve session, latency, SEL/SDR or reachability anomalies

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It issues only OOB `mc info`, leaves N undefined, hardcodes cipher 17, exposes the password, discards successful stdout because of redirection order, and omits in-band commands, SEL/SDR mix, 12-hour scheduling, per-request evidence and health recovery.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use two explicitly identified OOB/in-band read-only generators with an approved command distribution and token-bucket rate/concurrency bounds, capturing every completion and independent SEL/SDR/FRU/dmesg/reachability evidence for 12 hours.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The example `mc info`, `sel elist`, `sdr elist`, dual OOB/IB paths and 720-minute duration remain; exact path implementation and safe load envelope require owner confirmation.

modernized_recommendation.status: DUAL-PATH BMC READ-LOAD SOAK WITH SESSION AND LATENCY GOVERNOR
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Tag each request by access path and command class, rate-limit both generators, reserve health/recovery sessions and correlate latency/completion tails with BMC services, SEL and OS events.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the mass-load quantity bounded and auditable, separates OOB from in-band behavior and protects the very recovery channel being stressed.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An OOB-only `mc info` burst can pass while in-band transport, SEL enumeration or SDR service fails; aggregate success counts can also hide latency collapse and session exhaustion.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Sustained reads can exhaust BMC sessions, starve web/Redfish/IPMI services and impair recovery; management-network behavior may dominate results if the path is not isolated.

project_override_considerations: Approve whether `IB` means host in-band IPMI and identify its transport, exact OOB/in-band command mix, rate/concurrency/session reserve, cipher policy, allowable latency/error percentiles, reachability cadence and recovery escalation.
expected_evidence: Approved dual-path topology, command/load plan, BMC firmware, tool versions and secure session policy
Calibration and immutable per-request path/command/timestamp/latency/completion records
Request-rate, concurrency, active-session and reachability timelines for the full 12 hours
Periodic complete SEL/SDR/FRU/BMC health and preserved incremental dmesg/syslog/OS events
No write-command audit, threshold/abort/no-retry evidence and session cleanup
Final normal BMC functionality/latency, OS health, recovery readiness and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure, 12-hour Machine Time and Criteria consistently define sustained BMC command load with OOB plus IB paths and event-health acceptance. `IB` requires owner path definition but does not contradict the BMC-stress objective.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The read-only BMC stress purpose, example commands, duration and criteria are clear. Paths and safe load limits are identifiable inputs, so classification is REQUIRES rather than BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Restores OOB and in-band command diversity, converts unspecified mass load into governed per-request evidence and prevents the test from exhausting or obscuring the management/recovery channel it is meant to validate.
independent_technical_reasoning: BMC degradation often appears first in tail latency or session allocation, not total request failure. If the generator retries aggressively, it can amplify the fault and erase the distinction between service slowdown and network loss. Rate governance, reserved monitoring sessions and path-labeled completion codes are needed to show the BMC remained functional under load rather than merely recovered afterward.
